data.standardized_narrative: The syndicate recorded gross adverse prior-year reserve development of approximately GBP 10.4m (about 15.5% of opening gross claims outstanding of GBP 67.049m), driven by adverse development in older underwriting years (notably 2011-2013 columns in the gross claims development table). Management narratively notes a small net improvement on prior year reserves on a net-of-reinsurance basis driven by favourable Property run-off which was offset by unfavourable development in Political Risk and Consumer Products lines. Named catastrophe events cited as drivers of adverse development include earthquakes (Chile and New Zealand) and major weather events (e.g. Japanese earthquake, Thailand floods, Hurricane Irene, US tornadoes, Superstorm Sandy), primarily impacting the Property portfolio.
raw_causal_phrases: Included within net claims incurred of GBP 48.0m (2014: GBP 48.3m) is an improvement of GBP 0.2m (2014: improvement of GBP 9.4m) to claims reserves established at the prior year end principally due to the favourable Property run-off offset by unfavourable development for Political Risk and Consumer Products business.

The ultimate loss for the 2010 year of account has been driven primarily by poor performance in the Property account. Significant Catastrophe losses arising from earthquakes in Chile and New Zealand were incurred.

The ultimate loss for the 2011 year of account has primarily been driven by poor performance in the Property account arising from exposure to the Japanese earthquake, Thailand floods, Hurricane Irene, US tornadoes and Superstorm Sandy.

data.data_quality_notes: Prior-year development (10.4) was calculated from the gross claims development triangle (gross basis) by comparing the current estimate to the previous diagonal for underwriting years <= 2013. The Technical Provisions note provides a 'movement in provision' line that mixes current-year movements and is not appropriate for PYD per the extraction rules. The textual disclosure cites a small net improvement (GBP 0.2m) on a net-of-reinsurance basis; gross movement therefore differs from narrative net figure. There are RITC transactions referenced elsewhere (closure/reinsurance-to-close of earlier years) which can distort development tables; use of the triangle is a best-effort extraction but subject to that distortion risk.
